fixes.explanation: That's the one. John says, "And the dragon gave the beast his power and his throne and great authority." The dragon is the devil and Satan (Revelation 12:9). So the power, the throne and the authority were all handed to it.

Michael is the angel who fought the dragon (Revelation 12:7), so he's on the other side of this story. John says the one who gave the beast its power, throne and authority was the dragon. Michael shows up in the chapter before, so I can see how the name might come to mind.

Spreading would make this a sadder story for the beast, but that's not what John sees. He says, "…the mortal wound was healed…" The wound is healed instead of growing. Hold onto that word, because the whole world reacts in the next part of the verse.
You've got it. John says, "…the mortal wound was healed, and the whole world marveled and followed the beast." First the wound is healed. Then the whole world marvels, and it follows.

The text says the opposite. John writes, "…the mortal wound was healed, and the whole world marveled and followed the beast." So the wound is healed, the whole world marvels, and the world follows. Nobody turns away in this verse.

That's how the crowd's words come across. They ask, "Who is like the beast, and who can wage war against it?" It's a question with an answer already built in: nobody. And just before this, the verse says the whole world marveled and followed the beast (Revelation 13:3).
Seventy is a nice round number, but it's not the one in the verse. John says "…authority to act for 42 months." That's the number the text gives. The time is given, and it's 42.

The dragon is the one who gave the beast its power (Revelation 13:2), so this guess makes sense. But John says the beast speaks "…blasphemies against God…" The people also worship the dragon along with the beast (Revelation 13:4).

A lamb and a shepherd go together nicely, which makes this one tempting. But the verse says the beast "…had two horns like a lamb, but spoke like a dragon." Nothing here says it sounds like a shepherd. It spoke like a dragon.

Healing does show up in this chapter, when the first beast's wound was healed (Revelation 13:3), so I see the mix-up. But for the second beast, John says the signs let it deceive "…those who dwell on the earth…" The word the verse uses is deceived.

Warns is a fair guess for something called a sign. But John says the beast "…deceived those who dwell on the earth…" The signs it was given to perform on behalf of the first beast are the reason the verse gives. So deceives is the word.
That's the word. The second beast "…was permitted to give breath to the image of the first beast, so that the image could speak…" Notice "permitted" again. The text says it was allowed to do this.
